name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t maintenance—it’s Reel choking on malformed JSON from kimtaeyoon83’s scraper when YouTube’s API shifts. Forking the tool in-house while running Kaedim’s paid API in parallel for critical videos settles the argument: we hit 100% coverage today without betting the farm on a dead repo.

name: Scope
text:
**DO:** Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on all 10 pending videos today.

**WHY:** It’s the only free, open-source tool that delivers clean JSON with timestamps and speaker IDs—no paywall, no extra formatting. Speed is the trade-off, but we hit 100% coverage today without locking into a paid API.

**RISK:** If YouTube’s API shifts and breaks the scraper, we’ll lose time—but we’ll still have the raw video data to reprocess later. Forking now adds delay; we’ll patch only if the tool fails.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk is that kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript will fail mid-run, leaving us with partial or corrupted data and no fallback—YouTube’s API shifts break scrapers monthly, and this one hasn’t been updated in 8 months. A better alternative is to run Kaedim’s paid API in parallel for all 10 videos today, then compare outputs; if the free tool’s JSON matches Kaedim’s for 90% of the data, we keep it for future batches and deprecate Kaedim.
